name: golden
description: Reference-quality answers for the `smoke` fault set. Used to prove the blind-eval lane scores a competent operator answer as PASS. Fixture answers are contract evidence only — never model-behavior evidence.

FAULT-001.rootCause: The Postgres password secret was rotated to an invalid credential, so the application can no longer authenticate to the database.
evidenceCited: FATAL: password authentication failed surfaced through Npgsql.PostgresException
connection refused from the database endpoint
error_rate spike while db_connection_pool_active drops to 0
request_duration_seconds increases across database-backed routes
readiness probe fails while the liveness probe may still pass initially
remediationSteps: Restore the previous secret version in the secrets manager
Restart the workload after the secret update so the connection pool re-authenticates
FAULT-001.rollbackPlan: If the restore is wrong, re-apply the newer secret version in the secrets manager and restart the workload again.
verificationSteps: Verify the secret version is correct in the secrets manager
Confirm the connection pool recovers and error_rate returns to baseline

FAULT-002.rootCause: The database security group no longer admits application traffic, so every Postgres connection from the app subnet times out; this is a network connectivity block, not a credential problem.
evidenceCited: timeout expired and connection timed out in application logs
could not connect to server
db_connection_errors increases while active_connections drops
request_duration_seconds spikes on database-backed routes
readiness probe fails after connection pool drains while liveness may pass
remediationSteps: Re-add the security group ingress rule that admits the application security group on the Postgres port
Verify VPC peering and subnet routing between the application and database tiers
FAULT-002.rollbackPlan: Remove the ingress rule again through Terraform or the AWS CLI if the change widens exposure beyond the application security group.
verificationSteps: Verify connectivity restored from an application task to the database endpoint
Confirm the connection pool recovers and db_connection_errors returns to zero

FAULT-003.rootCause: The Redis auth token no longer matches the value the application presents, so every cache connection is rejected at authentication and the cache is effectively unavailable.
evidenceCited: NOAUTH Authentication required and ERR invalid password in the logs
StackExchange.Redis.RedisConnectionException on cache calls
cache_hit_ratio drops to 0 while cache_errors increases
request_duration_seconds increases on cached endpoints
readiness probe may pass because the cache is optional, with degraded performance
remediationSteps: Update the Redis auth token so it matches the value the application presents
Restart the application after the credential fix so pooled connections re-authenticate
FAULT-003.rollbackPlan: Restore the previous Redis auth token and restart the application if the updated token is rejected.
verificationSteps: Verify cache connectivity from the application
Confirm the hit ratio recovers and cache_errors returns to zero

FAULT-004.rootCause: The configured Redis endpoint hostname does not resolve, so this is a DNS misconfiguration of the cache endpoint rather than an authentication or capacity failure.
evidenceCited: No such host is known and DNS resolution failed in the logs
SocketException raised on every cache call
cache_errors increases alongside dns_resolution_failures increases
readiness probe may pass if the cache is non-critical
remediationSteps: Correct the REDIS_ENDPOINT environment variable to the real cache hostname
Verify DNS resolution from the workload network before redeploying
FAULT-004.rollbackPlan: Restore the previous Redis endpoint value in the environment config if the corrected hostname is also unreachable.
verificationSteps: Verify DNS resolution of the cache hostname from inside the workload
Confirm cache connectivity and that dns_resolution_failures stops increasing

FAULT-005.rootCause: The ingress load balancer target group points at the wrong backend port, so the ALB has no healthy upstream and returns 502 for every external request.
evidenceCited: upstream connect error and no healthy upstream
502 status from ALB on external requests
alb_healthy_host_count drops to 0 while 5xx_count increases
external health check fails while internal health checks may still pass
remediationSteps: Correct the target group port configuration to the container listen port
Verify the ALB listener rules forward to the corrected target group
FAULT-005.rollbackPlan: Restore the previous target group port via Terraform if the corrected port also fails to register healthy targets.
verificationSteps: Verify ALB target health transitions to healthy after the port correction
Confirm 5xx_count returns to baseline on the external listener

FAULT-006.rootCause: A readiness regression in the newly deployed revision makes the ALB target unhealthy, so the rolling deployment stalls and traffic is served by the previous revision at reduced capacity.
evidenceCited: health check failed followed by target deregistration
ECS task stopped during the rollout
healthy_host_count drops while ecs_task_failures increases
readiness probe returns 5xx or timeout
remediationSteps: Rollback to the previous task definition revision to restore capacity
Fix the readiness endpoint and redeploy once the regression is understood
FAULT-006.rollbackPlan: ECS service rollback to the previous task definition, which is the known-healthy revision.
verificationSteps: Verify the new task definition passes health checks in a lower environment first
Confirm healthy_host_count returns to the expected target count
